references.title: IFO-VGIC: Irregular Forced Opening of Voltage-Gated Ion Channels by electromagnetic fields
references.finding: Comprehensive review of 131 studies. 95% report oxidative effects from RF/Wi-Fi exposure. IFO-VGIC mechanism: polarized, coherent RF-EMF forces S4 voltage sensor to oscillate at non-physiological frequency, causing irregular channel opening, uncontrolled Ca2+ influx, ROS, DNA damage, sperm disorders, hormonal changes. VGIC blockers prevent effects, confirming mechanism.

references.authors: Bertagna F, Lewis R, McArthur S, Bhatt DK
references.title: Electromagnetic fields modulate neuronal membrane ionic currents through altered cellular calcium homeostasis
references.journal: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences
references.finding: 50 Hz, 1 mT, 60 min ELF-EMF on mouse hippocampal CA1 pyramidal neurons. Inward currents ↓40%, transient outward ↓50%. Two independent Ca²⁺ pathways identified: (1) RyR (ryanodine receptor) — dantrolene blocked EMF effects; (2) SERCA (sarco/endoplasmic reticulum Ca²⁺-ATPase) — CPA blocked EMF effects. Both intracellular Ca²⁺ store pathways abrogate EMF-induced ionic current changes, extending IFO-VGIC mechanism to include intracellular calcium dynamics.

references.authors: Koivisto M, Revonsuo A, Krause C et al.
references.title: Effects of 902 MHz electromagnetic field emitted by cellular telephones on response times in humans
references.finding: Two double-blind RCTs (2000a: n=48, 30 min; 2000b: n=48, 60 min). 902 MHz GSM left-sided exposure. Facilitation of cognitive performance (3-Back RT decrease in 2000a; Simple RT, Vigilance, Subtraction in 2000b). Compatible with acute VGIC activation at non-thermal SAR. Note: not replicated (Haarala 2003, 2005).

references.authors: Eliyahu I, Luria R, Hareuveny R et al.
references.title: Effects of radiofrequency radiation emitted by cellular telephones on the cognitive functions of humans
references.finding: n=36, 890.2 MHz, 2h bilateral exposure (Nokia 5110, 2W peak). Left-sided exposure slowed left-hand RT in spatial recognition task. Lateralization supports BERM two-channel spatial structure: EMF effect localizes to the exposed hemisphere. Compatible with local VGCC activation (pathway A) and local BBB opening (pathway E, cf. Salford 2003).

references.authors: Luria R, Eliyahu I, Hareuveny R et al.
references.title: Cognitive effects of radiation emitted by cellular phones
references.finding: n=48 right-handed males, 890.2 MHz, 1h, SAR 0.54-1.09 W/kg (Nokia 5110). Right-hand RT increased during left-sided exposure (first 2 blocks only). Time-dependent adaptation compatible with Selye GAS dynamics (alarm to resistance), which BERM pathway D (HPA to HPG) models at chronic timescale. Male-only sample matches BERM bioCap target population.

references.title: Wi-Fi is an important threat to human health
references.finding: 28 studies show calcium channel blockers prevent EMF effects. VGCC voltage sensor has 7.2 million times higher sensitivity than thermal prediction.

references.title: Proton dynamics in voltage-gated calcium channel selectivity filter
references.finding: Grotthuss proton hopping in VGCC selectivity filter provides quantum-level mechanism for EMF sensitivity at non-thermal intensities.

references.title: Nerve cell damage in mammalian brain after exposure to microwaves from GSM mobile phones
references.finding: BBB permeability increased at SAR 0.016 W/kg — 100× below safety limits. Neuronal damage in cortex, hippocampus, basal ganglia.

references.title: Oxidative mechanisms of biological activity of low-intensity radiofrequency radiation
references.finding: 93 of 100 peer-reviewed studies reported oxidative stress increases at sub-thermal RF levels. Confirms VGCC→Ca²⁺→ROS pathway.

references.title: Ameliorative Role of Coenzyme Q10 in RF Radiation-Associated Testicular and Oxidative Impairments in a 3.5-GHz Exposure Model
references.finding: Rats exposed to 3.5 GHz (5G core frequency) RF radiation showed testicular and oxidative damage. CoQ10 supplementation ameliorated these effects. First 5G-frequency-specific testicular data. CoQ10 rescue demonstrates mechanism reversibility, consistent with BERM recovery window concept. Testis antiox capacity decreased under RF.

references.title: Umbrella review of EMF biological effects
references.finding: 39 systematic reviews confirm biological effects of non-thermal EMF exposure across multiple endpoints.

references.title: Resonance effects indicate a radical-pair mechanism for avian magnetic compass
references.finding: RF at Larmor frequency disrupts magnetic compass in birds. Confirms radical pair mechanism. Disruption threshold ~15 nT.

references.title: Anthropogenic electromagnetic noise disrupts magnetic compass orientation in migratory birds
references.finding: Man-made electromagnetic noise in 2 kHz–5 MHz band disrupts compass orientation. Shielding restores it. First demonstration of anthropogenic EMF ecological impact.

references.title: The radical pair mechanism of magnetoreception
references.finding: RPM is the leading hypothesis for magnetoreception. Cryptochrome radical pairs sensitive to Earth-strength magnetic fields.

references.title: Low-intensity electromagnetic fields induce human cryptochrome to modulate intracellular reactive oxygen species
references.finding: Pulsed EMF induces CRY-dependent ROS modulation in human HEK293 cells and mouse embryonic fibroblasts at non-thermal intensities. CRY is the transducer.

references.authors: Chae K-S, Oh I-T, Lee S-H, Kim S-C
references.title: Blue light-dependent human magnetoreception in geomagnetic food orientation
references.finding: Starved men orient toward geomagnetic food-associated directions (P<0.001). Requires blue light (<500 nm), confirming radical pair mechanism via cryptochrome. Inclination compass confirmed. First behavioral evidence of functional CRY/RPM magnetoreception in humans.

references.title: Gender is a major factor explaining discrepancies in eye colour prediction
references.finding: Males more likely blue-eyed; females show higher green and brown frequencies. Same genotype produces darker eyes in females (X-chromosome mosaicism).

references.title: Sex tweaks eye color
references.finding: X-chromosome mosaicism mechanism for sex difference in eye color. Women have fewer extreme colors (blue, dark brown) and more intermediate (green, hazel).

references.title: Cryptochrome mediates light-dependent magnetosensitivity in Drosophila
references.finding: CRY mutants do not respond to magnetic fields. Wild-type does. Confirms CRY as magnetoreception transducer.

references.title: FAD-superoxide radical pair mechanism in cryptochrome
references.finding: CRY FAD-superoxide radical pair responds to Earth-strength fields via asymmetric recombination.

references.authors: Hirano A, Braas D, Fu Y-H, Ptáček LJ
references.title: FAD Regulates CRYPTOCHROME Protein Stability and Circadian Clock in Mice
references.finding: FAD stabilizes CRY1/CRY2. B2-deficient diet + RFK knockdown decreases CRY levels and alters circadian gene expression.

references.authors: Yap JLY, Tai YK, Franco-Obregón A et al.
references.title: Magnetically Stimulated Myogenesis Recruits a CRY2-TRPC1 Photosensitive Signaling Axis
references.finding: RFK silencing (FAD depletion) attenuates PEMF responses and inhibits magnetic field directional selectivity. CRY2-TRPC1 physical interaction confirmed. Reveals A-C pathway coupling.

references.authors: Nießner C, Denzau S, Peichl L, Wiltschko W, Wiltschko R
references.title: Magnetoreception in birds: I. Immunohistochemical studies concerning the cryptochrome cycle
references.finding: CRY1a activation spectrum: UV-green (373-565nm). Oxidized CRY absorbs to 500nm; semiquinone absorbs to 570nm. Green light maintains but cannot initiate activation.

references.authors: Bartölke R, Nießner C, Reinhard K, Wolfrum U, Meimann S, Bolte P, Feederle R, Mouritsen H, Dedek K, Peichl L, Winklhofer M
references.title: Full-Length Cryptochrome 1 in the Outer Segments of the Retinal Blue Cone Photoreceptors in Humans and Great Apes Suggests a Role Beyond Transcriptional Repression
references.finding: Full-length CRY1 protein found exclusively in outer segments of short-wavelength-sensitive blue cone photoreceptors in human, bonobo, and gorilla retinas. Location suggests non-circadian, phototransductive function.

references.authors: Majewska M, Hanić M, Bartölke R, Schmidt J, Bożek J, Gerhards L, Mouritsen H, Koch K-W, Solov'yov IA, Brand I
references.title: European Robin Cryptochrome-4a Associates with Lipid Bilayers in an Ordered Manner, Fulfilling a Molecular-Level Condition for Magnetoreception
references.finding: ErCry4a associates with model lipid membranes in uniform, partially restricted orientation. Membrane lamellae provide orientational order required for directional magnetoreception.

references.title: Non-monotonic magnetic field effects in planarians confirm RPM predictions
references.finding: RPM non-monotonic predictions confirmed in planarian worms. Biological compass effects measurable in simple organisms.

references.title: EMF effects on pineal melatonin production
references.finding: EMF exposure suppresses pineal melatonin production. Melatonin regulates GnRH pulsatility.

references.title: Light at night, chronodisruption, melatonin suppression, and cancer risk
references.finding: Melatonin suppression → GnRH disruption → HPG axis dysregulation → reproductive consequences.

references.authors: Wacker J, Frühauf J, Schulz M, Chiwora FM, Volz J, Becker K
references.title: Riboflavin deficiency and preeclampsia
references.finding: B2-deficient mothers had 4.7× higher preeclampsia risk (OR 4.7, CI 1.8-12.2). Intracellular free FAD was significantly lower in preeclampsia patients.

references.title: EMF exposure and corticosterone elevation in rodents
references.finding: EMF exposure elevated corticosterone with large effect size d=1.88. Confirms chronic HPA axis activation.

references.title: EMF exposure and depression risk
references.finding: EMF exposure associated with depression OR 1.45. HPA-mediated mood dysregulation.

references.title: Mobile phone use and salivary cortisol
references.finding: Mobile phone use >2h/day associated with elevated salivary cortisol. N=200.

references.title: A population-level decline in serum testosterone levels in American men
references.finding: Age-independent T decline 1.2%/yr 1987-2004. Persists after BMI/smoking/health control.

references.authors: Santi D, Spaggiari G, Furini C, Griseta V, Zizzi EA, Granata ARM, Simoni M
references.title: Temporal trends in serum testosterone and luteinizing hormone levels indicate an ongoing resetting of hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal function in healthy men: a systematic review
references.finding: Largest meta-analysis (n=1,064,891, 1971-2024). Both T and LH declining independent of age, BMI, and assay method. First to show simultaneous T and LH decline, indicating HPG-level disruption. No BMI temporal trend in this population.

references.title: Decline in serum testosterone in adolescents and young adults
references.finding: T decline particularly severe in younger males. Suggests environmental cause.

references.title: Meta-analysis: EMF effects on testosterone (29 animal studies)
references.finding: EMF → T↓, SMD 0.87 (95% CI 0.43-1.30), mean SAR 0.9 W/kg.

references.title: Testosterone is associated with mating success but not attractiveness or masculinity in human males
references.finding: T correlates with mating success via courtship effort, not physical attractiveness. T makes men more active approachers, not more attractive.

references.title: Exogenous testosterone influences sexual overperception bias
references.finding: Exogenous T increases tendency to interpret women's signals as sexual interest. T↓ → reduced overperception → fewer approaches. RCT.

references.title: Testosterone causes both prosocial and antisocial status-enhancing behaviors in human males
references.finding: Exogenous T causally increases status-seeking behavior. Not just aggression but strategic social behavior. RCT confirms causal direction.

references.title: The dual-hormone hypothesis for social status
references.finding: T effects on status behavior manifest ONLY when cortisol is low. High cortisol blocks T behavioral expression. EMF raises cortisol AND lowers T → double lock.

references.title: Meta-analysis of dual-hormone hypothesis (30 studies, N=8538)
references.finding: T×cortisol interaction significant for status-relevant behavior (r=-.061, p=.026).

references.title: Human fluctuating asymmetry and sexual behavior
references.finding: Women attracted to T-produced traits (masculinity, symmetry) as signals of genetic quality.

references.title: The polyvagal theory: phylogenetic substrates of a social nervous system
references.finding: Myelinated vagus inhibits HPA and enables social engagement. Chronic stress → vagal suppression → OT↓ → social bonding↓.

references.title: Oxytocin and vasopressin in the evolution of sociality
references.finding: OT/AVP fundamental neuropeptides enabling mammalian sociality, pair bonding, and parental behavior.

references.title: Oxytocin and social affiliation in humans
references.finding: OT functions as biobehavioral synchronizer in parent-infant bonding and pair formation.

references.title: Probiotic microbes sustain youthful serum testosterone levels and testicular size in aging mice
references.finding: L. reuteri → T↑, testicular weight↑, spermatogenesis↑, Leydig cells↑. Mechanism: IL-17 suppression.

references.title: Microbes and oxytocin: benefits for host physiology and behavior
references.finding: L. reuteri upregulates OT via vagus nerve. Immune-endocrine-brain signaling network.

references.title: Microbial symbionts accelerate wound healing via oxytocin
references.finding: L. reuteri accelerates wound healing through OT upregulation. Gut microbiome modulates systemic OT.

references.title: Wi-Fi exposure alters gut microbiome composition in mice
references.finding: Wi-Fi exposure changed Firmicutes/Bacteroidetes ratio. EMF directly alters gut microbiome.

references.title: Membrane potential drives spermatogonial stem cell differentiation via mTOR
references.finding: Vmem depolarization → mTOR activation → premature SSC differentiation → stem cell pool exhaustion.

references.title: Depolarization of sperm membrane potential in infertile men
references.finding: 10% of infertile men show fully depolarized Vmem. Direct link between bioelectric state and fertility.

references.title: Bioelectricity as a universal signaling mechanism
references.finding: Bioelectric signaling (Vmem patterns) is a universal mechanism controlling cell behavior, morphogenesis, and regeneration.

references.title: Temporal trends in sperm count: a systematic review and meta-regression analysis
references.finding: Sperm concentration declined 52.4% from 1973-2011 among Western men.

references.title: Temporal trends in sperm count: updated meta-regression
references.finding: Decline accelerated: −62% from 1973-2018. Global (not just Western). No sign of plateau.

references.title: Radiofrequency electromagnetic radiation and sperm quality
references.finding: RF-EMR from mobile phones reduces sperm motility, viability, and increases DNA fragmentation.

references.title: Is fertility reduced among men exposed to radiofrequency fields in the Norwegian Navy?
references.finding: OR 1.86 for infertility in RF-exposed Navy personnel. Dose-response. Sex ratio shift. N=10,497.

references.title: Calcium channel blockers and male fertility
references.finding: CCBs (nifedipine, amlodipine) reduce sperm motility and acrosome reaction in clinical use. Confirms VGCC→fertility pathway.

references.title: Rapamycin (mTOR inhibitor) effects on fertility

Note: EMP is high-amplitude short-duration, different from BERM's chronic low-intensity RF exposure. Mechanistic relevance: same molecular target (tight junctions) as Salford 2003 GSM study.

references.title: Scoping review: electromagnetic field effects on blood-brain barrier permeability
references.authors: IOP Science (Physics in Medicine and Biology)
references.finding: Evidence contradictory but positive results replicated in multiple independent labs (Salford, Tang, Ulusoy, Gao). Negative results partly explained by measurement method differences.

references.title: Short-term RF-EMF application as non-invasive tool for targeted BBB modulation
references.journal: Iranian Journal of Basic Medical Sciences
references.finding: 30 min RF-EMF at 27.12 MHz significantly increased eNOS gene expression and decreased occludin — without oxidative stress or inflammation. Longer exposures (180, 360 min) produced HIF-1a increase, claudin-1 and occludin decrease, and histopathological edema. The mechanism is eNOS-mediated vasodilation + TJ protein downregulation. Confirms BBB opening mechanism is TJ-protein mediated (occludin, claudin-1) — the same proteins as in BTB.

references.title: Electromagnetic field treatment protects against and reverses cognitive impairment in Alzheimer transgenic mice
references.finding: 918 MHz EMF (2h/day) disaggregates Aβ oligomers, enhances mitochondria, reverses cognitive decline in AD mice. BBB opening beneficial in clean blood context.

references.title: Age-related changes in blood-brain barrier tight junction protein expression in mice
references.finding: Aged mice (24 months vs 3 months): occludin significantly decreased, ZO-1 decreased, TNF-α elevated in brain endothelial cells, capillary permeability significantly increased.

references.title: 900 MHz EMF exposure impairs spatial memory and increases BBB permeability in rats
references.finding: 900 MHz, 3h/day, 28 days → spatial memory impairment AND BBB permeability increase in rat hippocampus and cortex. Mechanism: mkp-1/ERK pathway. Below safety standards.

references.title: 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi exposure affects brain microRNA expression below safety limits
references.finding: 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi well below legal limit → significant changes in brain microRNA expression. Long-term 2.4 GHz exposure may lead to adverse effects including neurodegenerative diseases via miRNA changes.

references.title: Mobile phone radiation activates hsp27/p38MAPK stress response in human endothelial cells
references.finding: 900 MHz activates hsp27/p38MAPK stress response in human endothelial cells. Hypothesis: hsp27 activation may increase BBB permeability via endothelial stress fiber stabilization.

references.title: Calcium hypothesis of Alzheimer's disease and brain aging: A framework for integrating new evidence
references.finding: Ca²⁺ dysregulation is a PROXIMAL CAUSE of Alzheimer's dysfunction. Intracellular calcium changes precede and drive amyloid pathology, not the reverse.

references.title: Effect of calcium on Aβ(1-40) aggregation: toxic oligomers vs. harmless fibrils
references.finding: In the presence of Ca²⁺, Aβ(1-40) preferentially forms TOXIC OLIGOMERS rather than harmless fibrils. Calcium level determines whether amyloid is dangerous or not.

references.title: Alzheimer's disease: A short review of the role of calcium in early events
references.finding: Ca²⁺ dysregulation is an EARLY event in AD that precedes neurodegeneration. Calcium signaling changes occur before clinical symptoms.

references.title: Calcium homeostasis and neuronal excitability in Aβ neurotoxicity
references.finding: Ca²⁺ homeostasis and neuronal excitability are key factors in Aβ neurotoxicity. Disruption of calcium regulation amplifies amyloid toxicity.

references.title: Presenilin mutations and calcium dysregulation in Alzheimer's disease
references.finding: PSEN1/PSEN2 mutations (familial AD) cause Ca²⁺ dysregulation genetically. Demonstrates genetic convergence on the same calcium pathway that EMF activates environmentally.

references.title: Why anti-amyloid therapies have not lived up to their promise
references.finding: Anti-amyloid drugs remove plaques but do NOT improve cognition. Plaques are a symptom, not the cause. Need alternative mechanistic hypotheses for AD.

references.title: Prenatal exposure to magnetic field nonionizing radiation and the risk of ADHD in offspring
references.authors: Li DK, Chen H, Ferber JR, Hirst AK, Odouli R
references.finding: 1482 mother-child pairs with objective MF measurement (24h dosimetry). High prenatal MF → ADHD risk ↑, especially persistent/severe ADHD and ADHD with immune comorbidities. Dose-response relationship. Modifiable risk factor.

references.title: CACNA1C in psychiatric disorders: comprehensive review of GWAS associations
references.finding: CACNA1C rs1006737 repeatedly associates with bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, MDD, ADHD, and ASD in GWAS. Same gene/channel that modulates EMF sleep sensitivity (Sousouri 2025).

references.title: CACNA1C gene and vulnerability to neuropsychiatric disorders
references.finding: Comprehensive review of CACNA1C Cav1.2 role across psychiatric diagnoses. VGCC dysfunction is a convergence point for multiple neurodevelopmental and psychiatric disorders.

references.title: CACNA1C gain-of-function equivalent to Timothy syndrome alters axon targeting and behavior
references.finding: Timothy syndrome CACNA1C gain-of-function (G406R) causes autism with high penetrance. VGCC overactivity = autistic phenotype. Channel function directly regulates neural network development.

references.title: Alpha2A-adrenoceptors strengthen working memory networks by inhibiting cAMP-HCN channel signaling in prefrontal cortex
references.finding: Guanfacine mechanism: α2A → cAMP↓ → HCN channels close → membrane potential stabilized → PFC signal-to-noise ratio improves. Direct ion channel intervention for ADHD, not neurotransmitter modulation.

references.title: Fetal radiofrequency radiation exposure from 800-1900 MHz-rated cellular telephones affects neurodevelopment and behavior in mice
references.authors: Aldad TS, Gan G, Gao X-B, Taylor HS
references.finding: 800-1900 MHz fetal exposure in mice → neurodevelopmental and behavioral changes. Experimental confirmation of Kaiser Permanente epidemiological findings.

references.title: Prenatal mobile phone exposure affects cognition in aged rat offspring
references.finding: Prenatal mobile phone exposure → cognitive decline in AGED rat offspring. Effect is LIFELONG, not transient. Supports permanent calibration error hypothesis.

references.title: CACNA1A and autism spectrum disorders
references.finding: CACNA1A (P/Q-type VGCC) variants associate with ASD. Expressed in cortex, cerebellum, hippocampus. Multiple VGCC subtypes implicated in neurodevelopmental disorders.

references.title: Rare CACNA1H variants in autism spectrum disorder families
references.finding: 53 rare CACNA1H (T-type Cav3.2) variants identified in 40 ASD families. T-type calcium channel dysfunction contributes to ASD risk.

references.title: Involvement of voltage-gated calcium channels in early brain development
references.finding: VGCCs are critical for brain DEVELOPMENT, not just function. Channel expression regulates neural migration, synaptogenesis, and network formation during critical windows.

references.title: Ion channel conductance changes underlie bipolar neuron excitability oscillations
references.finding: Bipolar hippocampal neurons oscillate between hyperexcitability and hypoexcitability due to Na⁺ current decrease + K⁺ current increase. Li-responsive neurons are hyperexcitable (stable, correctable); Li-nonresponsive are UNSTABLE (oscillating).

references.title: Na,K-ATPase hypothesis of bipolar disorder
references.finding: MILD Na,K-ATPase dysfunction → excitability ↑ → MANIA. MORE SEVERE dysfunction → neurotransmitter release ↓ → DEPRESSION. Two levels of the SAME ionic disruption produce OPPOSITE clinical states.

references.title: Potassium channels in bipolar disorder
references.finding: Comprehensive review of K⁺ channel roles in bipolar disorder. Multiple potassium channel genes implicated in mood regulation and bipolar risk.

references.title: Leukemia cells hijack stromal cell bioelectricity via CaV1.2 depolarization
references.finding: Leukemia cells 'hijack' stromal cell bioelectricity through CaV1.2 depolarization. Direct evidence that cancer manipulates ion channel bioelectricity for survival.

references.title: Vagus nerve stimulation inhibits cytokine production and attenuates disease severity in rheumatoid arthritis
references.finding: VNS activates α7nAChR (ligand-gated ion channel) → NF-κB ↓ → TNF-α ↓ → significant response in rheumatoid arthritis. Direct ionic intervention for autoimmune disease.

references.title: Verapamil inhibits breast cancer cell growth in vitro
references.finding: Verapamil (VGCC L-type blocker) inhibits breast cancer cell growth in vitro. Ion channel modulation as anti-cancer strategy.

references.title: PI3K/AKT → GSK3β → KCNQ2 pathway in bipolar disorder
references.finding: PI3K/AKT → GSK3β → KCNQ2 signaling pathway links lithium's mechanism to potassium channel regulation in bipolar disorder.

references.authors: Tong J, Sheng S, Sun Y, et al.

references.title: The role of melatonin as an antioxidant in the follicle
references.finding: Follicular fluid melatonin correlates with oocyte quality; melatonin acts as critical antioxidant protector of oocytes

references.title: Systematic review of melatonin effects on oocyte and embryo quality in IVF
references.finding: Systematic review confirms melatonin supplementation improves oocyte quality, embryo development, and IVF success rates

references.title: Meta-analysis of melatonin supplementation and clinical pregnancy rate in IVF
references.finding: Meta-analysis: melatonin supplementation significantly improves clinical pregnancy rate in IVF

references.title: Melatonin and female reproductive function: five mechanistic pathways
references.finding: Review: melatonin affects female fertility via HPG axis, antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, mitochondrial, and epigenetic pathways

references.authors: Wilson BW, Anderson LE, Hilton DI, Phillips RD

references.finding: Melatonin protects sperm from oxidative damage, regulates HPG axis, and modulates seasonal reproduction

references.authors: Unfer V, Raffone E, Riber P, et al.

references.finding: Melatonin + myo-inositol improves oocyte quality in IVF; small N, blinding challenges

references.authors: Nishihara T, Hashimoto S, Ito K, et al.
references.title: Oral melatonin supplementation improves human sperm motility
references.finding: Melatonin supplementation improves sperm motility in vitro and in vivo

references.title: Radiofrequency electromagnetic fields and melatonin: epidemiological review
references.finding: Review of RF-EMF and melatonin suppression in humans: inconsistent results, plausible mechanism

references.authors: Higuchi S, Motohashi Y, Ishibashi K, Maeda T
