references.journal: Am J Physiol Regul Integr Comp Physiol
references.finding: Light-eyed Caucasians: 89% melatonin suppression. Dark-eyed Asians: 73%. Eye pigmentation directly modulates circadian light pathway.

references.title: Systematic review of intermediate frequency electromagnetic field animal studies
references.finding: IF range (300 Hz - 10 MHz) systematically under-researched compared to ELF and RF. Studies on health effects with more diverse perspectives of IF-EMF have NOT been conducted. Regulatory gap confirmed.

references.authors: University of the West Indies research group
references.title: Effects of 150 kHz intermediate frequency electromagnetic radiation on rat reproductive parameters
references.finding: 150 kHz IF-EMR 8 weeks: testicular mass decrease (p=0.03), interstitial cell count decrease (p=0.01), FSH increase (p=0.01), sperm trajectory changes (p=0.05). 150 kHz is within LED driver emission range.

references.authors: Kim J, Hwang Y, Kim S, Kwon D, Park J et al.
references.title: Electromagnetic field-inducible in vivo gene switch for remote spatiotemporal control of gene expression
references.finding: 60 Hz 2 mT pulsed EMF activates Lgr4 gene promoter in vivo via Cyb5b mitochondrial outer membrane protein producing rhythmic Ca2+ oscillations. CRISPR-identified mechanism. Reversible. Published in Cell (IF ~64). Contested by York (New Scientist): incredibly implausible.

references.authors: Duraccio KM, Zaugg KK, Langeveld RC, Jensen CD
references.title: Blue light filtering does not improve sleep outcomes in adolescents
references.finding: Blue-light-filtering glasses did NOT significantly improve adolescent sleep quality. Suggests non-optical component (IF emissions from screens/LED lighting) may be more important than blue light for sleep disruption.

references.title: Impact of electromagnetic fields on circadian rhythms: molecular and physiological insights
references.finding: PRISMA 2020 systematic review: 55 studies from 892 screened. 88% of high-quality animal studies report EMF-induced melatonin suppression (20-50% from baseline). Clock gene expression altered. Sleep architecture changes documented. Melatonin suppression smaller than light-induced (>90%). Only 27% of studies met high methodological standards.

references.title: Effect of iris pigmentation and latitude on chronotype and sleep timing
references.finding: Light-eyed subjects had earlier sleep times and more morningness. Iris pigmentation modulates circadian light sensitivity.

references.authors: Lamia KA, Sachdeva UM, DiTacchio L, Williams EC, Alvarez JG, Egan DF, Vasquez DS, Juguilon H, Panda S, Shaw RJ, Thompson CB, Evans RM
references.title: AMPK Regulates the Circadian Clock by Cryptochrome Phosphorylation and Degradation
references.finding: AMPK phosphorylates CRY1 at Ser71 triggering FBXL3-mediated ubiquitin degradation. AMPK activity was rhythmic and inversely correlated with CRY1 nuclear protein abundance.

references.title: Dirty electricity, chronic stress, neurotransmitters and disease
references.finding: Library intervention: reducing kHz-range IF transients changed urinary dopamine and PEA in 7 volunteers. N=7 pilot, low evidence level, but mechanism consistent with IF affecting neurotransmitter pathway.

references.title: Dirty electricity elevates blood sugar among electrically sensitive diabetics
references.finding: kHz-range transients elevated blood glucose in electrosensitive diabetic patients. GS filters reduced both IF transients and blood glucose. Small N, controversial author. Mechanism consistent with K-ATP channel hypothesis.

references.title: Tumor Treating Fields (TTFields) FDA approval for glioblastoma
references.finding: 200 kHz alternating electric fields disrupt mitotic spindle and destroy cancer cells. FDA-approved for glioblastoma (2011, 2015). Operating frequency (200 kHz) in same range as LED driver emissions (20-300 kHz). If 200 kHz intentionally disrupts cell division, environmental 200 kHz from LED drivers may do so unintentionally.

references.title: Fertility and ageing
references.finding: Comprehensive review of declining fertility trends across industrialized nations, documenting age-specific and cohort-specific fertility decline patterns

references.authors: Neuhaus E, Zirjacks L, Ganser K ym.
references.title: Alternating Electric Fields (TTFields) Activate Cav1.2 Channels in Human Glioblastoma Cells
references.finding: 200 kHz TTFields activate Cav1.2 (L-type VGCC) calcium channels in glioblastoma cells. Ca2+ entry, cell cycle arrest, mitochondrial membrane potential breakdown. Cav1.2 knockdown blunts effect. Same channel as Sousouri 2025 CACNA1C.

references.authors: Gera N, Yang A, Holber SC ym.
references.title: Mitotic Spindle Disruption by Alternating Electric Fields Leads to Improper Chromosome Segregation and Mitotic Catastrophe in Cancer Cells
references.finding: TTFields disrupt mitotic spindle via tubulin dimer dipole moment interference. Leads to chromosome missegregation and mitotic catastrophe. Mechanism: dielectrophoretic forces at cleavage furrow.

references.authors: Sato Y, Taki M, Kojimahara N
references.title: Association Between the Use of Induction Heating Cookers and Delivery Outcomes in Pregnant Women
references.finding: Statistically significant OR 1.27-1.44 for preterm birth with stationary/tabletop IH cookers. DOSE-RESPONSE: higher IF emission (9 mT) -> higher OR than lower (4 mT built-in). Internet-based cohort, Japan.

references.authors: Tokinobu A, Tanaka K, Arakawa M, Miyake Y
references.title: Maternal Use of Induction Heating Cookers During Pregnancy and Birth Outcomes: The Kyushu Okinawa Maternal and Child Health Study
references.finding: 1565 mothers, Kyushu cohort. IH cooker use associated with REDUCED preterm birth risk (contradicts Sato 2023). Difference likely due to IH type classification: Tokinobu did not separate high-emission vs low-emission cookers.

references.authors: Sato Y, Kiyohara K, Takehara S, Kojimahara N
references.title: Ecological study on the penetration of induction heating cookers and birth outcomes in Japan
references.finding: 47 prefectures. No significant association at ecological level. Weak positive association with fetal death after 22 weeks. Ecological design too coarse for individual-level exposure.

references.authors: Li DK, Odouli R, Wi S ym.
references.title: A population-based prospective cohort study of personal exposure to magnetic fields during pregnancy and the risk of miscarriage
references.finding: EMDEX-measured 24h MF exposure during pregnancy. Miscarriage risk doubled (OR ~2.0) above 1.6 mG. Dose-response relationship. Kaiser Permanente cohort.

references.authors: Li DK, Ferber JR, Odouli R, Quesenberry CP
references.title: A Prospective Study of In-utero Exposure to Magnetic Fields and the Risk of Childhood Obesity
references.finding: 733 children followed to age 13. Prenatal high MF exposure -> childhood obesity risk OR 1.69. 33 weight measurements per child on average. Kaiser Permanente.

references.authors: Li DK, Chen H, Odouli R
references.title: Maternal Exposure to Magnetic Fields During Pregnancy in Relation to the Risk of Asthma in Offspring
references.finding: Prenatal MF exposure associated with offspring asthma risk. EMDEX-measured. Kaiser Permanente cohort.

references.title: Exposure to magnetic fields and the risk of poor sperm quality
references.finding: Higher daily MF exposure >1.6 mG associated with 2-fold risk of poor sperm quality (abnormal motility and morphology). Dose-response relationship with duration.

references.authors: Khan MW, Roivainen P, Herrala M, Tiikkaja M, Sallmen M, Hietanen M, Juutilainen J
references.title: A pilot study on the reproductive risks of maternal exposure to magnetic fields from electronic article surveillance systems
references.finding: Finnish supermarket cashiers exposed to EAS (58 kHz). No significant differences in miscarriage, birth weight, or preterm birth. Could not differentiate EAS technology types. Authors recommend kHz-specific studies.

references.authors: Yamaguchi-Sekino S, Taki M, Ikuyo M ym.
references.title: Assessment of combined exposure to intermediate-frequency electromagnetic fields and pulsed electromagnetic fields among library workers in Japan
references.finding: EAS gates in libraries produce elliptically polarized IF magnetic fields. Chronic occupational exposure documented. Rotating fields may specifically affect melatonin.

references.title: Measurement and Exposure Assessment of Intermediate Frequency Magnetic Fields From Electronic Article Surveillance (EAS) Gates in Libraries
references.finding: Detailed IF-MF measurements from 5 EAS gate models. Transient and chronic exposure quantified. Induced electric field numerically calculated for human body models.

references.authors: Herrala M, Kumari K, Koivisto H ym.
references.title: Behavioral testing of mice exposed to intermediate frequency magnetic fields indicates mild memory impairment
references.finding: 7.5 kHz MF (EAS frequency), 120 uT, 5 weeks. Mild memory impairment in mice.

references.title: Early Exposure to Intermediate-Frequency Magnetic Fields Alters Brain Biomarkers without Histopathological Changes in Adult Mice
references.journal: Int J Environ Res Public Health
references.finding: 21 kHz 3.8 mT prenatal exposure -> NMDA receptor (NR1, NR2B), CaMKIV, CREB1, COX2, IL-1b, TNF-a, HO-1 all significantly increased in 7-week-old mice hippocampus. REVERSIBLE after exposure cessation.

references.title: Comparison of pulsed and continuous electromagnetic field generated by WPT system on human dermal and neural cells
references.finding: WPT system (87-207 kHz, 1.01-1.05 kW, 1.3-1.7 mT) tested on 4 human cell lines. Pulsed vs continuous exposure comparison.

references.authors: Blackman CF, Benane SG, House DE
references.title: The influence of temperature during electric- and magnetic-field-induced alteration of calcium-ion release from in vitro brain tissue
references.finding: Ca2+ efflux from brain tissue occurred at 36C and 37C but NOT at 35C, 38C, or 39C. The DIRECTION of effect (enhancement vs. reduction vs. null) depended on whether temperature was rising, stable, or falling during exposure. Three different outcomes — all genuine — from the same EMF dose at different temperatures. Demonstrates that 1C temperature difference changes the result from positive to null to negative.

references.authors: Blackman CF, Benane SG, House DE, Elliott DJ
references.title: Importance of alignment between local DC magnetic field and an oscillating magnetic field in responses of brain tissue in vitro and in vivo
references.finding: The relative orientation between the local DC magnetic field (geomagnetic) and the oscillating AC magnetic field is crucial for calcium release. Results are consistent with a magnetic resonance-like transduction mechanism. Labs in different geographic locations (different geomagnetic declination and inclination) and different building orientations get systematically different results at the same AC field parameters.

references.title: Long-term exposure to 4G smartphone RF-EMR diminished male reproductive potential by directly disrupting Spock3-MMP2-BTB axis
references.finding: Long-term exposure to 2605 MHz (4G) RF-EMR gradually damaged spermatogenesis and resulted in time-dependent reproductive toxicity by directly disrupting blood-testis barrier integrity via the Spock3-MMP2-BTB axis. The effect was progressive — consistent with a positive feedback mechanism where BTB opening increases exposure of protected tissue. First direct demonstration of BTB disruption by telecom-frequency RF.

references.title: All four voltage-sensing domains of human CaV3.1 activate within a narrow voltage range near resting membrane potential
references.finding: All four voltage-sensing domains of human CaV3.1 (T-type) activate within a narrow voltage range near resting membrane potential (-70 to -50 mV). Solves the longstanding conundrum of how T-type channels achieve low-voltage sensitivity. Establishes that T-type channels are maximally sensitive NEAR resting potential — the exact range where EMF-induced perturbations via Schwan equation are largest.

references.title: ClC-2 facilitates T-type VGCC-mediated steroidogenesis in Leydig cells
references.finding: In Leydig cells, ClC-2 chloride channels facilitate membrane depolarization that activates voltage-gated calcium channels. Inhibition of T-type VGCC attenuated cAMP-induced steroidogenic gene expression and testosterone synthesis. ClC-2 knockdown in vivo diminished intratesticular testosterone levels. Completes the chain: EMF -> Schwan dVm -> T-type Cav3 -> Ca2+ -> StAR -> testosterone.

references.title: Cav1 and Cav3 are both essential for spermatogenesis
references.finding: Functional regulation of Cav channels is essential for normal spermatocyte development. Inhibition of Cav1 (L-type, nifedipine) or Cav3 (T-type, ethosuximide) disrupts normal spermatogenesis and steroidogenesis during prepubertal testicular maturation. Both channel types required — EMF perturbation of T-type window current provides chronic low-level disruption mechanism.

references.title: The Effect of 2.45 GHz RF-EMR on Components of the HPG Axis in Male Rats
references.finding: 2.45 GHz RF-EMR disrupts multiple components of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal (HPG) axis in male rats, including GnRH pulsatility, pituitary gonadotroph FSH/LH secretion, and downstream gonadal function. Demonstrates that EMF affects the HPG axis at the pituitary level, not only at the gonadal level.

references.title: Biological Effects of Exposure to RF-EMF on the Placental Barrier in Pregnant Rats
references.finding: RF-EMF exposure affects placental barrier integrity in pregnant rats, suggesting that biological barriers beyond BBB and BTB are vulnerable to EMF-induced tight junction disruption. Extends the barrier vulnerability model to the placental barrier during pregnancy.

references.title: Cell phone EMF exposure increases systolic blood pressure and plasma renin activity
references.finding: Cell phone EMF exposure increases systolic blood pressure and plasma renin activity, indicating autonomic cardiovascular effects mediated through the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system. Supports the autonomic/cardiovascular pathway of EMF biological effects.

references.title: Low Intensity EMFs Act via VGCC Activation to Cause Very Early Onset Alzheimer's: 18 Distinct Types of Evidence
references.finding: Presents 18 distinct types of evidence that low-intensity EMFs act via voltage-gated calcium channel (VGCC) activation to produce very early onset Alzheimer's disease. The Ca2+ hypothesis of AD converges with EMF-VGCC pathway: EMF → VGCC → Ca2+ influx → BACE1 activation → amyloid-beta production → neurodegeneration.

references.title: Do electromagnetic fields significantly affect thyroid cells and their functions? A systematic review
references.finding: Systematic review examining whether electromagnetic fields significantly affect thyroid cells and their functions. Evidence suggests EMF exposure can alter thyroid hormone levels and thyroid cell function, contributing to hypothyroidism and TSH dysregulation through VGCC-mediated and endocrine disruption pathways.

references.title: Effects of 4G LTE EMF on Thyroid Hormone Dysfunction and Behavioral Changes in Adolescent Male Mice
references.finding: 4G LTE EMF exposure causes thyroid hormone dysfunction and behavioral changes in adolescent male mice. Demonstrates disruption of the hypothalamic-pituitary-thyroid (HPT) axis with downstream effects on DIO2 enzyme activity and thyroid hormone conversion, supporting the endocrine disruption pathway of EMF effects.

references.title: Genome-wide sperm DNA methylation alterations in individuals exposed to radar electromagnetic radiation
references.finding: Genome-wide analysis reveals significant sperm DNA methylation alterations in radar-exposed individuals, identifying differentially methylated regions relevant to transgenerational epigenetic effects of electromagnetic radiation.

references.title: Effect of 50 Hz ELF-EMF on DNA Methylation and DNA Methyltransferases in Mouse Spermatocyte-Derived Cell Line GC-2
references.journal: PMC (Int J Environ Res Public Health)
references.finding: 50 Hz ELF-EMF alters DNA methylation and DNMT1/DNMT3B expression in GC-2 spermatocyte cells with non-monotonic dose-response and window effects, suggesting epigenetic modulation at specific intensity windows.

references.title: Whole-body RF-EME exposures cause DNA damage in mouse spermatozoa via oxidative mechanism
references.finding: Whole-body RF-EME exposure at 905 MHz causes DNA damage in mouse spermatozoa via mitochondrial ROS generation and elevated 8-OHdG, demonstrating an oxidative mechanism for RF-induced sperm genotoxicity.

references.title: Genotoxic Risks to Male Reproductive Health from Radiofrequency Radiation
references.finding: Review of genotoxic risks from RF radiation to male reproductive health, covering sperm 8-OHdG elevation, DNA fragmentation, and transgenerational germline effects across multiple studies.

references.title: The essential calcium channel of sperm CatSper is temperature-gated
references.finding: CatSper, the essential calcium channel of sperm, is temperature-gated with a thermal threshold at 33.5C, linking temperature sensing to capacitation and establishing CatSper as a thermosensitive ion channel relevant to reproductive physiology.

references.title: Association between mobile phone use and semen quality: decreasing association over time
references.finding: Association between mobile phone use and semen quality decreases over time, with stronger effects during GSM era compared to LTE, suggesting modulation type (not just SAR) influences biological outcomes — consistent with Schwan membrane coupling hypothesis.

references.title: T-type calcium channel blockade reduces StAR and testosterone in prepubertal mouse Leydig cells
references.finding: T-type calcium channel blocker ethosuximide reduces StAR mRNA, testosterone production, and Leydig cell number in prepubertal mice. LH unchanged — direct effect, not HPG axis. Pharmacological proof that T-type Ca²⁺ channels control testosterone synthesis.

references.title: Mibefradil inhibits steroidogenic gene expression in MA-10 Leydig cells
references.finding: T-type blocker mibefradil reduces StAR, Cyp11a1, Hsd3b1, Cyp17a1 mRNA in MA-10 Leydig cells. Testosterone production significantly decreased. Confirms T-type Ca²⁺ dependence of entire steroidogenic pathway.

references.title: CACNA1C variants associated with five major psychiatric disorders
references.finding: GWAS mega-analysis (33,332 cases, 27,888 controls): CACNA1C variants significantly associated with all five major psychiatric disorders — ASD, ADHD, bipolar, MDD, schizophrenia. Single gene, five phenotypes.

references.title: Timothy syndrome G406R CACNA1C mutation causes autism via disrupted axon targeting
references.finding: Timothy syndrome G406R gain-of-function mutation in CACNA1C causes autism with 80% penetrance. Mechanism: excessive Ca²⁺ influx disrupts axon targeting via selective autophagy → circuit formation defects.

references.title: Central precocious puberty increase in Denmark 1998-2017
references.finding: Central precocious puberty (CPP) increased 3× in girls and 2× in boys in Denmark 1998-2017. CPP girls had significantly lower salivary melatonin, linked to electronic device EMF exposure.

references.title: ASD-gender dysphoria comorbidity in large clinical datasets
references.finding: 6-26% of autistic individuals report gender-atypical feelings. TriNetX 48k dataset confirms ASD-GD clustering. AFAB 22% gender-nonconforming. Consistent with shared CACNA1C vulnerability.

references.title: OXTR expression develops in two waves: perinatal and pubertal
references.finding: OXTR expression develops in two waves: perinatal (stronger in males) and pubertal. OT modulates interoception in insular cortex. VGCC-dependent Ca²⁺ influx required for OT release from magnocellular neurons.

references.title: Oxytocin modulates interoceptive attention in insular cortex
references.finding: OT regulates attention switching between interoceptive and exteroceptive signals in insular cortex. Disrupted OT → altered body-self relationship. Adolescent interoceptive processing is still developing — context-dependent and variable.

references.title: Alpha-fetoprotein protects female fetal brain from estrogen masculinization
references.finding: Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) binds circulating estrogen, protecting female fetal brain from masculinization. AFP does NOT bind testosterone. Local brain aromatase can produce estradiol that bypasses AFP protection.

references.title: Brain aromatase (CYP19) expression requires Ca²⁺-dependent MAPK phosphorylation
references.finding: Aromatase expression requires MAPK1/3 phosphorylation which depends on extracellular calcium. Demonstrated in granulosa cells, derived for neurons. Brain aromatase converts testosterone to estradiol in sexually dimorphic regions.

references.authors: Jimenez H, Wang M et al.
references.title: Tumour-specific AM RF EMF induce differentiation of HCC via targeting Cav3.2 T-type VGCC and Ca2+ influx
references.finding: FDA-approved TheraBionic device treats HCC via non-thermal EMF targeting Cav3.2 T-type calcium channels. Amplitude-modulated 27.12 MHz at SAR 100-1000x below mobile phone levels induces Ca2+ influx and tumor cell differentiation.

references.title: HDE H220001: TheraBionic P1 Summary of Safety and Probable Benefit
references.finding: FDA Humanitarian Device Exemption for TheraBionic P1 treating advanced HCC. Label explicitly contraindicates calcium channel blockers, confirming Ca2+ mechanism. 34% survival increase in advanced HCC.

references.authors: Lu M, Xian F et al.
references.title: Upregulation of Cav1.3 in IHCs by IL-6-dependent inflammaging contributes to age-related hearing loss
references.finding: IL-6-dependent inflammaging upregulates Cav1.3 in inner hair cells, causing chronic Ca2+ overload and excitotoxicity at IHC synapses, contributing to age-related hearing loss.

references.title: Functional expression of T-type Cav3.2 in female and male human DRG neurons
references.finding: Cav3.2 T-type calcium channels are functionally expressed in human DRG nociceptors with sex-differential expression. Female DRG neurons show more prominent Cav3.2 currents.

references.title: Targeting T-type/CaV3.2 channels for chronic pain
references.finding: Cav3.2 is the primary pain channel in DRG nociceptors. Expression and activity are significantly upregulated in inflammatory and neuropathic pain models. T-type channel blockers are effective analgesics.

references.title: The CaV3.3 calcium channel is the major sleep spindle pacemaker in thalamus
references.finding: Cav3.3 knockout mice completely lack sleep spindles in the nucleus reticularis thalami (nRt). Cav3.3 is the major pacemaker for sleep spindle generation.

references.title: Thalamic Cav3.1 T-type Ca2+ channel plays a crucial role in stabilizing sleep
references.finding: Cav3.1 knockout mice show reduced delta waves and increased sleep fragmentation. Thalamic T-type channels are essential for sleep stability.

references.title: Investigation of CACNA1I Cav3.3 dysfunction in hemiplegic migraine
references.finding: CACNA1I burden test shows OR 2.30 (P=0.00005) for hemiplegic migraine. T-type Cav3.3 dysfunction contributes to cortical spreading depression.

references.title: The clinical spectrum of FHM associated with mutations in a neuronal Ca channel
references.finding: CACNA1A gain-of-function mutations cause familial hemiplegic migraine type 1. Increased Ca2+ influx leads to excessive glutamate release and cortical spreading depression.

references.authors: Park YJ, Yoo SA et al.
references.title: The role of Ca2+-calcineurin-NFAT signaling pathway in health and autoimmune diseases
references.finding: Ca2+-calcineurin-NFAT pathway is critical for T-cell activation. Pharmacological inhibitors (cyclosporine, tacrolimus) are standard autoimmune treatments, confirming that Ca2+ dysregulation drives autoimmunity.

references.title: Global and Chinese epidemiologic study of PCOS in women of childbearing age, 1990-2021, projections to 2035
references.finding: PCOS prevalence is 5-20% of reproductive-age women and rising through 2035. Global analysis shows increasing trend aligned with metabolic and environmental changes.

references.title: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and long QT syndrome in cardiac-only Timothy syndrome
references.finding: CACNA1C gain-of-function mutations cause Timothy syndrome with cardiac manifestations including long QT syndrome and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Window current increase drives action potential prolongation.

references.title: A CACNA1C variant associated with reduced VDI, increased Cav1.2 window current, and arrhythmogenesis
references.finding: CACNA1C variants that reduce voltage-dependent inactivation increase the Cav1.2 window current, prolonging cardiac action potentials and causing arrhythmias. Window current is a key pathogenic mechanism.

references.title: Role of light in eye growth and light as therapy for myopia control
references.finding: Dopamine release from amacrine cells acts as a brake on scleral elongation. Light exposure is protective against myopia via this DA pathway. Circadian regulation of ocular growth is CRY-dependent.

references.title: Oxytocin receptor expression patterns in the human brain across development
references.finding: Oxytocin receptor expression in the human brain shows sex-differential developmental trajectories. OXTR expression peaks during critical periods of social brain development.

references.title: Oxytocin modulation of the insular cortex: implications for social cognition and neurodevelopmental disorders
references.finding: Oxytocin modulates insular cortex activity, linking it to interoception, body awareness, and social cognition. Disruption during development may contribute to altered body representation.

references.title: Early androgen exposure and human gender development
references.finding: Prenatal androgen exposure shapes human gender development. CAH females exposed to high prenatal androgens show more masculine behavior and gender identity patterns.

references.title: Androgens and the masculinization programming window: human-rodent differences
references.finding: The masculinization programming window (MPW) is a critical period when androgens program male reproductive tract development. AGD is a biomarker of MPW androgen action. Phthalate disruption during MPW causes TDS.

references.title: Pediatric autoimmune diseases in the light of COVID-19 pandemic
references.finding: Pediatric autoimmune disease incidence increased during and after COVID-19 pandemic. T1D, celiac disease, and psoriasis showed significant increases in children.

references.title: TRN parvalbumin neurons regulate sleep spindles and electrophysiological aspects of schizophrenia
references.finding: TRN parvalbumin neurons regulate sleep spindle generation via T-type calcium channels. Reduced spindle density is a biomarker of schizophrenia, linking Cav3.3 dysfunction to psychiatric disease.

references.title: The Environment and Disease: Association or Causation?
references.finding: Established nine criteria for evaluating causal associations in epidemiology: strength, consistency, specificity, temporality, biological gradient, plausibility, coherence, experiment, analogy.

references.title: Smoking and Health: Report of the Advisory Committee to the Surgeon General
references.journal: US Department of Health, Education, and Welfare
references.finding: Landmark report establishing causal link between smoking and lung cancer using Bradford Hill criteria. Demonstrated that systematic application of causal criteria can overcome industry resistance to scientific evidence.

references.title: Coronary atherosclerosis in indigenous South American Tsimane: a cross-sectional cohort study
references.finding: Tsimane have the lowest reported levels of coronary artery disease of any population recorded to date. CT angiography showed 85% of Tsimane adults had no coronary artery calcium, compared to only 14% of Americans of the same age.

references.title: Prevalence of dementia and mild cognitive impairment in indigenous Bolivian forager-horticulturalists
references.finding: Dementia prevalence among Tsimane is approximately 1.2%, compared to 8-11% in the US and Europe. Moseten (partially modernized, shared ancestry) show intermediate rates, suggesting a modernization gradient.

references.title: Brain volumetric deficits in a forager-horticulturalist population: the Tsimane
references.finding: Tsimane brain atrophy rate is approximately 70% slower than in Western populations of the same age. Parieto-occipital regions show growth rather than decline in older Tsimane males.

references.title: Hunter-gatherers as models in public health
references.finding: Hadza and other hunter-gatherer populations show near-absence of obesity, T2D, and cardiovascular disease despite diverse diets and activity patterns, suggesting environmental rather than purely dietary drivers.

references.title: Apparent absence of cerebrocardiovascular disease in Melanesians
references.finding: Kitava islanders (Papua New Guinea) show apparent absence of stroke, ischaemic heart disease, diabetes mellitus, and metabolic syndrome despite a high-carbohydrate diet (70% energy from tubers and fruit).

references.title: Amish fertility in the United States
references.finding: Old Order Amish maintain TFR of approximately 6.1 (vs. US national 1.66), with slight decline from 6.9 in 1924 to 6.1 in 2014. Communities reject smartphones and limit electrical technology use.

references.title: Cancer incidence in the Amish of Ohio
references.finding: Overall cancer rates among Ohio Amish are approximately 60% of the age-adjusted rate for non-Amish Ohio residents. Tobacco-related and non-tobacco-related cancers are both reduced.

references.title: Mental health among the Amish
references.journal: J Amish and Plain Anabaptist Studies
references.finding: Depression rates among Old Order Amish communities are consistently reported below 1%, compared to approximately 8% in the general US population. Strong community structure is a likely co-factor.

references.title: Optimal levels of physical activity and consumption for brain aging in Tsimane and Moseten
references.finding: Tsimane and Moseten form a natural modernization gradient with shared genetic background. Moseten health outcomes fall between Tsimane and Western populations on measured variables, consistent with a dose-response to modernization.

references.title: Global myopia prevalence trends: rural Africa 1.4-11.4%, Latin America 1.4-14.4%, East Asia 80-95% in youth
references.finding: Myopia prevalence follows a five-level gradient that tracks technology adoption and urbanization: rural Africa (1-11%), Latin America (1-14%), Europe (17-36% youth), USA (~50% youth), East Asia (80-95% youth). COVID screen time increase produced a measurable myopia spike in children.

references.title: Cav1.3α1 L-type channels activate at substantially more negative voltages and have longer open times than Cav1.2α1
references.finding: Cav1.3 L-type channels activate at approximately −50 mV, about 25 mV more negative than Cav1.2. This makes Cav1.3 a low-threshold L-type channel with greater EMF sensitivity than canonical Cav1.2.

references.title: L-type CaV1.2 calcium channels: from in vitro findings to in vivo function
references.finding: Cav1.2 requires strong depolarization (approximately −30 mV) for activation, meaning it opens primarily during action potentials, not at resting membrane potential. This contrasts with Cav3 T-type and Cav1.3 channels.

references.title: Molecular physiology of low-voltage-activated T-type calcium channels
references.finding: T-type (Cav3) channels are the primary low-voltage-activated calcium channels, with window currents operating near resting membrane potential. This makes them uniquely susceptible to subthreshold voltage perturbations including EMF-induced fields.

references.title: T-type calcium channels: key features for resting potential operation
references.finding: T-type channels have a unique window current that allows baseline calcium influx at resting membrane potential (−70 mV). This resting-state activity is critical for the BERM bifurcation model.

references.title: VGCC modulation by kinases: CaMKII shifts T-type activation threshold
references.finding: CaMKII phosphorylation shifts Cav3.2 activation threshold to more negative potentials, creating a positive feedback loop: Ca²⁺ → CaMKII → lower threshold → more Ca²⁺. This mechanism explains cumulative EMF sensitization.

references.title: Automated electrophysiology: VGCC pharmacological selectivity of DHP, phenylalkylamine, and benzothiazepine
references.finding: Dihydropyridine (DHP) blockers including amlodipine and nifedipine are highly selective for L-type (Cav1.2) channels with LOW affinity for T-type channels. This selectivity is critical for interpreting VGCC blocker experiments.

references.title: Congenital deafness and sinoatrial node dysfunction in mice lacking class D L-type Ca2+ channels
references.finding: Cav1.3 knockout mice are congenitally deaf and have sinoatrial node dysfunction, proving Cav1.3 is essential for both hearing (inner hair cell synaptic transmission) and cardiac pacemaking.

references.title: T-type window currents at resting potential in human myometrium
references.finding: T-type calcium channels produce measurable window currents at resting membrane potential in human myometrium, with half-activation at −46 mV. Demonstrates T-type resting-state activity in reproductive tissue.

references.title: T-type window currents allow baseline Ca²⁺ influx and membrane depolarization at rest in VTA neurons
references.finding: T-type window currents provide baseline Ca²⁺ influx at resting potential in VTA dopamine neurons. Blocking T-type channels hyperpolarizes these neurons, proving resting-state T-type activity drives tonic calcium entry.

references.authors: Andersson AM, Jensen TK, Juul A, et al.
references.title: Secular decline in male testosterone and SHBG serum levels in Danish population surveys
references.finding: Cohort-dependent decline in testosterone and SHBG in Danish men, independent of age and BMI

references.authors: Chodick G, Epstein S, Shalev V
references.title: Secular trends in testosterone: findings from a large state-mandate care provider
references.finding: Declining testosterone in 102,334 Israeli men (2006-2019), age-independent

references.title: Meta-analysis of secular trends in testosterone: 54% decline across 6 longitudinal studies
references.finding: Pooled analysis shows 54% total testosterone decline across multiple longitudinal cohorts with accelerating trend

references.title: The global decline in sperm count and testosterone levels: trends, mechanisms, and environmental drivers
references.finding: Comprehensive review confirming 1.2%/year testosterone decline globally with environmental drivers including EMF

references.title: Male reproductive disorders and fertility trends: influences of environment and genetic susceptibility
references.finding: Testicular dysgenesis syndrome links cryptorchidism, testicular cancer, hypospadias, and declining sperm/T to environmental exposures

references.authors: Mazur A, Westerman R, Mueller U
references.title: Is rising obesity causing a secular (age-independent) decline in testosterone among American men?
references.finding: Weight-stable men lost 117 ng/dL (19%) over 20 years. Excludes obesity as sufficient explanation for secular T decline. 991 US Air Force veterans, 6 waves 1982-2002.

references.title: Mobile Phone Radiation Deflects Brain Energy Homeostasis and Prompts Human Food Ingestion
references.finding: RF-EMF acute exposure increased food intake in humans. 2h/day prepubertal rats showed appetite increase and weight gain at 3 weeks, continuing through 5-22 weeks.

references.title: Dose- and Time-Dependent Effects of RF-EMF on Adipose Tissue: Implications of Thermoregulation and Mitochondrial Signaling
references.finding: 900 MHz at SAR 0.1-0.4 W/kg reduced BAT thermogenesis and mitochondrial activity. Effects were dose- and time-dependent.

references.title: 5G Radiofrequency Exposure Reduces PRDM16 and C/EBPbeta mRNA Expression, Two Key Biomarkers for Brown Adipogenesis
references.finding: 3.5 GHz 5G exposure reduced PRDM16 by 49% and C/EBPbeta by 32% — key brown adipocyte differentiation markers. Age- and exposure-duration independent.

references.title: Prenatal WiFi exposure effects on body weight and behavior in rats
references.finding: Prenatal WiFi exposure increased body weight and caused behavioral hyperactivity in male rats. Suggests metabolic programming.

references.title: RF-EMF effects on thyroid-mediated metabolism
references.finding: RF-EMF may affect metabolism through thyroid axis disruption, mediated via pituitary thyrotroph Cav3 channels affecting TSH secretion.

references.title: EMF effects on pancreatic function
references.finding: EMF exposure disrupts pancreatic beta-cell function and insulin secretion dynamics.

references.title: Direct modulation of GFAP-expressing glia in the arcuate nucleus bi-directionally regulates feeding
references.finding: Ca2+ activation of ARC glia increased AgRP/NPY neuron activity and food intake. Ca2+ disruption decreased food intake. Direct Ca2+ to appetite link.

references.title: Astrocytes control food intake by inhibiting AGRP neuron activity via adenosine A1 receptors
references.finding: Astrocyte stimulation in medial basal hypothalamus reduced ghrelin-evoked food intake via adenosine A1 receptor pathway.

references.title: Evidence That Ca2+ within the Microdomain of the L-Type VGCC Activates ERK in MIN6 Cells in Response to GLP-1
references.finding: GLP-1 activates ERK through L-type VGCC Ca2+ microdomain in beta-cells. Sustained ERK activation requires continual L-type VGCC activation.

references.title: VGCC alpha2delta-1 subunit regulates glucose-stimulated GLP-1 secretion
references.journal: Am J Physiol Gastrointest Liver Physiol
references.finding: VGCC alpha2delta-1 is highly expressed in intestinal L-cells. Gabapentin (alpha2delta inhibitor) reduced GLP-1 secretion, confirming VGCC dependence.

references.title: Nifedipine increases energy expenditure by increasing PGC-1alpha expression in skeletal muscle
references.finding: Nifedipine (L-type VGCC blocker) decreased body weight gain ratio and white adipose tissue weight. Mechanism: PGC-1alpha upregulation in skeletal muscle.

references.title: Screen time increases overweight and obesity risk among adolescents: a systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis
references.finding: 44 studies: screen time OR 1.273 (95% CI 1.166-1.390) for overweight/obesity. Dose-response relationship confirmed.

references.title: Night-shift work and its association with metabolic syndrome
references.finding: Night-shift work associated with metabolic syndrome OR 1.17 (95% CI 1.02-1.35). Melatonin, cortisol, thyroid and sex hormones all affected.

references.authors: Trumble BC, Cummings D, von Rueden C, O'Connor KA, Smith EA, Gurven M, Kaplan H
references.title: Physical competition increases testosterone among Amazonian forager-horticulturalists: a test of the 'challenge hypothesis'
references.journal: Proceedings of the Royal Society B
references.finding: Tsimane baseline T 33% lower than US men but does NOT decline with age. Normal reactivity to competition (30% boost). Absent age-decline in zero-EMF population.

references.title: Effects of long-term treatment with testosterone on weight and waist size in 411 hypogonadal men with obesity classes I-III
references.finding: T therapy produced weight loss up to 30 kg in class III obesity. Confirms bidirectional T-BMI causation: T suppression drives weight gain, not just the reverse.

references.title: Age-Related Testosterone Decline and Metabolic Determinants in 27,687 Korean Men
references.finding: Mean T = 480 ng/dL (n=27,687). Biochemical hypogonadism 5.5% (40-49y) to 11.6% (70+y). First large Korean T dataset.

references.title: A cohort effect on serum testosterone levels in Finnish men
references.finding: Birth cohort effect: later-born men have lower T. LH and FSH ALSO declined in later cohorts. 3,271 men, BMI-adjusted. Independent Finnish confirmation of Santi 2025 LH finding.

references.title: Testosterone and cortisol jointly regulate dominance: Evidence for a dual-hormone hypothesis
references.finding: T→status-seeking behavior link is modulated by cortisol: relationship is stronger when cortisol is low and attenuated when cortisol is high. Establishes the dual-hormone hypothesis for dominance behavior.

references.title: Dual-hormone hypothesis meta-analysis
references.finding: Meta-analysis (n=8,538) confirms that cortisol modulates testosterone's effect on status-relevant behavior. The interaction is multiplicative: low T + high cortisol produces behavioral suppression greater than either alone.

references.title: Male labor force participation rate
references.finding: April 2026: US male labor force participation rate 67% — lowest since 1940s record-keeping began. Decline from 87% (post-war) to 67% has accelerated since 2010.

references.title: ELF-EMF exposure increases multiple VGCC subtypes
references.finding: ELF 8-10 days increases P/Q, N, R-type VGCC expression. Foundation for ELF priming hypothesis.

references.title: Sleep EEG alterations: exposure to pulsed radio frequency electromagnetic fields
references.finding: Modulation-specific sleep EEG effects. Effect proportional to peak power, not average — supports crest factor bioactivity.

references.title: Comparing DNA damage induced by mobile telephony and other types of man-made EMFs
references.finding: Pulsed fields more bioactive than CW. Mobile telephony EMFs include ELF components in pulsing patterns.

references.title: Temporal trends in sperm count: a systematic review and meta-regression analysis of samples collected globally in the 20th and 21st centuries
references.finding: Sperm concentration decline rate doubles post-2000: from 1.16%/yr to 2.64%/yr. Acceleration coincides with smartphone adoption.

references.title: Electromagnetic field exposure in electric vehicles
references.finding: EV EMF highest near inverter, driver and passenger seats. IF band (5-50 kHz) exposure significant.

references.title: Active electromagnetic field cancellation system for electric vehicles
references.finding: Patent US12379429 for active field cancellation in EV cabins. Industry acknowledges IF exposure concern.

references.title: WiFi is an important threat to human health
references.finding: WiFi crest factor 100:1 — peak power 100× average. May be more bioactive than other RF sources due to pulsing characteristics.

references.title: Intermediate frequency electromagnetic fields: research needs
references.finding: WHO and SCENIHR identify IF data as severely limited. Research designated as high priority. Gap between ELF and RF safety standards.

references.title: 150 kHz intermediate frequency exposure effects
references.finding: 150 kHz 2-month exposure: liver and lung effects in animal model. Demonstrates IF bioactivity at occupationally relevant frequency.

references.title: RF-EMF reduces bumblebee visitation to flowers
references.finding: RF electromagnetic field exposure reduces bumblebee flower visitation rates. Direct demonstration of RF impact on pollinator behavior.

references.title: Pineal melatonin level disruption in humans due to electromagnetic fields and ICNIRP limits
references.finding: ELF-MF suppresses melatonin in winter but increases it in summer in calves. Seasonally dependent effect supports CRY light-dependent sensitivity model.

references.title: Genetic variation in CACNA1C affects brain circuitries
references.finding: rs1006737 is a quantitative trait locus for CACNA1C transcript levels. A-allele increases Cav1.2 expression.

references.title: CACNA1C risk variant and amygdala activity in bipolar disorder, schizophrenia and healthy controls
references.finding: rs1006737 A-allele associated with altered amygdala activity across bipolar, schizophrenia AND healthy controls. Effect is genotype-dependent, not diagnosis-dependent.

references.title: CACNA1D de novo mutations in autism spectrum disorders
references.finding: Schizophrenia-associated CACNA1C variants also confer autism risk. Shared calcium channel vulnerability across neurodevelopmental disorders.

references.title: Changes in diet quality and weight status in the US population
references.finding: Americans eat fewer calories but weigh more since 2000. Caloric intake down, obesity up — the Mozaffarian paradox. Cannot be explained by diet alone.

references.title: Prevalence and ethnic pattern of diabetes and prediabetes in China in 2013
references.finding: China T2D prevalence: 1.3% (1980) to 8.7% (2014), a 17.3× increase. Trajectory parallels rapid electrification from 60% to 100%.

references.title: Global, regional, and national burden of diabetes from 1990 to 2021
references.finding: Post-COVID T2D EAPC accelerated from 2.90% to 3.52%. Lockdown increased indoor EMF exposure (WiFi+LED 24h/day) while eliminating recovery windows.

references.title: A comparison of temporal trends in United States autism prevalence to trends in suspected environmental factors
references.finding: 75-80% of autism increase is real, not diagnostic artifact. Most environmental toxins are flat or declining over the same period.

references.title: The origins of the obesity epidemic in the United States
references.finding: Obesity appeared simultaneously in 1976-80 across all genders, ages, and ethnicities — inconsistent with behavioral explanation, consistent with environmental exposure.

references.title: The trend of mean BMI values of US adults
references.finding: BMI acceleration periods coincided with radio adoption (1920s) and TV adoption (1950s). Each new broadcasting technology introduced new population-wide EMF exposure.

references.title: Electromagnetic radiation as an emerging driver factor for the decline of insects
references.finding: Sparrow density correlates negatively with EMF radiation. Urban decline 60%, rural decline 47% in UK.

references.title: Wood environments improve cognitive performance and reduce physiological stress
references.finding: Wood rooms: better sleep, lower heart rate, better cognition compared to concrete rooms. BERM adds RF-reflection mechanism to conventional biophilia explanation.

references.title: Shift work and metabolic syndrome: systematic review and meta-analysis
references.journal: Int J Environ Res Public Health
references.finding: Shift work MetS OR 2.17 (95% CI 1.31-3.60). 10/12 studies showed higher risk.

references.title: Shift work health effects: comprehensive review
references.finding: Shift workers: increased risks for diabetes, hypertension, CVD, MetS, mental health, cancer. IARC 2A for night shift. Endocrine: melatonin, cortisol, thyroid, sex hormones all affected.

references.title: Night shift work dose-response association with CVD
references.finding: Night shift work dose-response association with CVD incidence and mortality. 6 databases, meta-analysis.

references.title: Office work and cardiovascular risk factors
references.journal: Int J Environ Res Public Health
references.finding: Office workers: prolonged sedentary work tied to increased morbidity. Cardiovascular risk factors elevated. 1950s research: physically active work → lower CVD.

RF-EMF genotoxicity systematic review of 517 studies. Pulsed/real devices produce more effects than CW. Duration is critical factor. 58% of DNA damage effects observed below ICNIRP safety limits. Funding source predicts results more than study quality. U-shaped dose-response observed.
Systematic review of 55 studies on EMF and circadian disruption. 88% of high-quality animal studies show melatonin suppression. Human evidence varies considerably due to uncontrolled moderators.

ELF-EMF at 50 Hz and 35 µT with intermittent exposure caused DNA strand breaks in human fibroblasts. Damage reversed within 9 hours after exposure ceased. Effects observed well below ICNIRP 200 µT occupational limit.

5G at 3.6 GHz modulates sleep spindle frequency in CACNA1C genotype-dependent manner. T/C carriers show significant response while T/T carriers do not. Double-blind RCT demonstrating genetic susceptibility to RF-EMF.

WHO-commissioned systematic review of RF-EMF and fertility. 117 animal studies and 10 in vitro studies analyzed. Animal meta-analyses show adverse effects in all endpoints except infertile male rate and litter size.
Meta-analysis of mobile phone EMF and sperm quality. Phone use associated with reduced motility, viability, and concentration. Hedges g = -0.547 for motility.
3.5 GHz reduces sperm motility while 24 GHz reduces concentration and viability in rats. Effects amplified by 7h vs 1h daily exposure duration, confirming dose-duration relationship.
50 Hz 1 mT ELF-EMF for 85 days reduced sperm motility and testosterone in rats. Seminiferous tubule diameter decreased, confirming chronic ELF exposure affects male reproductive system.

references.authors: Küry S, van Woerden GM, Besnard T, et al.
references.title: De Novo Mutations in Protein Kinase Genes CAMK2A and CAMK2B Cause Intellectual Disability
references.finding: 19 de novo CAMK2A/B variants in 24 individuals with intellectual disability. Variants affecting Thr286/287 autophosphorylation produced epilepsy, ID, and ASD — the same phenotypes BERM predicts from environmental CaMKII dysregulation.

references.title: Homozygous loss-of-function CAMK2A mutation causes growth delay, seizures and severe intellectual disability
references.finding: Biallelic CAMK2A mutation causes defective oligomerization and failed neuronal rescue. Both GoF and LoF of CaMKII cause neurodevelopmental disorders, confirming precise regulation is critical.

references.authors: Patke A, Murphy PJ, Onat OE, et al.
references.title: Mutation of the Human Circadian Clock Gene CRY1 in Familial Delayed Sleep Phase Disorder
references.finding: CRY1Δ11 (c.1657+3A>C, rs184039278): gain-of-function variant with enhanced Clock/Bmal1 affinity, lengthened circadian period. Frequency 0.6%. Causes familial delayed sleep phase disorder.

references.authors: Lyssenko V, Nagorny CL, Erdos MR, et al.
references.title: Common variant in MTNR1B associated with increased risk of type 2 diabetes and impaired early insulin secretion
references.finding: rs10830963 G-allele predicts future T2D. MTNR1B mRNA is higher in risk carriers. Melatonin inhibits β-cell insulin secretion via MT2 receptor — EMF-induced melatonin changes differentially affect G/G carriers.

references.authors: Tuomi T, Nagorny CL, Singh P, et al.
references.title: Increased melatonin signaling is a risk factor for type 2 diabetes
references.finding: rs10830963 G → eQTL → increased MTNR1B expression → stronger melatonin inhibition of insulin. Daily melatonin accentuates repression in G/G carriers. Explains gene × environment interaction.

references.authors: Scholl UI, Stölting G, Nelson-Williams C, et al.
references.title: Recurrent gain of function mutation in calcium channel CACNA1H causes early-onset hypertension with primary aldosteronism
references.finding: CACNA1H GoF mutations cause aldosterone overproduction and hypertension. T-type calcium channel in adrenal cortex — gain-of-function lowers activation threshold.

references.title: Polymorphisms in CACNA1A, CACNA1C, and CACNA1H in Korean Pediatric Patients with Developmental Delay and Epilepsy
references.finding: CACNA1A rs16023 B-allele associated with developmental delay and epilepsy. Multi-gene calcium channel polymorphism interaction confirmed in Korean pediatric cohort.

references.title: WES identifies heterozygous CACNA1D variant associated with familial sinus node dysfunction and focal epilepsy
references.finding: CACNA1D R930H: sinus bradycardia + AV block + epilepsy + learning disability in one family. Isoform-specific GoF/LoF demonstrates Cav1.3 multi-organ role.

references.authors: Field MJ, Cox PJ, Stott E, et al.
references.title: Identification of the α2δ-1 subunit of voltage-dependent calcium channels as a molecular target for pain mediating the analgesic actions of pregabalin
references.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
references.finding: R217A mutant mice: pregabalin has no analgesic effect. α2δ-1 binding is necessary AND sufficient for analgesia. This identifies α2δ-1 as the molecular target shared by ELF priming and gabapentinoid therapy.

references.authors: Hoppa MB, Lana B, Marber W, Bhatt DK, et al.
references.title: α2δ expression sets presynaptic calcium channel abundance and release probability
references.finding: α2δ controls VGCC trafficking to presynaptic terminals. Overexpression of α1 alone does NOT increase synaptic VGCC levels — α2δ is the bottleneck. This is the molecular basis of ELF priming.

references.title: Observational study of CRY1 c.1657+3A>C variant: sleep-wake patterns and circadian metabolic output
references.finding: CRY1Δ11 carriers show later wake time, later midpoint of sleep, greater latency to persistent sleep, and later bowel movements. Confirms functional circadian lengthening in real-world conditions.

references.title: The melatonin receptor 1B gene links circadian rhythms and type 2 diabetes: an evolutionary story
references.finding: MTNR1B rs10830963 G associated with delayed melatonin offset, prolonged peak melatonin, and ethnic diversity consistent with thrifty gene hypothesis. Links circadian genetics to metabolic disease.

references.title: A perspective on neuropathologic findings in victims of the sudden infant death syndrome: the triple-risk model
references.finding: Triple risk model: vulnerable infant × critical developmental period × exogenous stressor. Foundation for modern SIDS research.

references.title: Cardiac ion channelopathies and the sudden infant death syndrome
references.finding: At least 1 in 5 SIDS victims carries an ion channel mutation. Majority have malignant phenotype when functionally characterized.

references.title: Genetic basis of sudden infant death syndrome: ion channel and cardiac arrhythmia genes
references.finding: RYR2 variants identified in 14% of post-mortem SIDS cases. CACNA1C underlies Timothy syndrome and Brugada syndrome phenotypes.

references.title: CACNA1C mutations in sudden infant death syndrome
references.finding: CACNA1C mutations associated with long QT syndrome and Brugada syndrome identified in SIDS post-mortem genetic screening.

references.title: Caffeine therapy for apnea of prematurity
references.finding: Caffeine citrate significantly reduces apnea episodes, bronchopulmonary dysplasia, and cerebral palsy in preterm infants. Landmark CAP trial.

references.title: Adenosine and dopamine receptor gene polymorphisms affect caffeine response in infant apnea
references.finding: ADORA1 and ADORA2A gene polymorphisms modulate caffeine efficacy in apnea of prematurity. Pharmacogenetic evidence linking adenosine-Ca2+ pathway to infant respiratory regulation.

references.title: Melatonin in human breast milk and its potential role in circadian entrainment
references.finding: Night breast milk contains melatonin and tryptophan. Breastfed infants achieve earlier circadian entrainment (6 weeks vs. 12 weeks), better sleep efficiency, and less colic.

references.title: Baby monitor RF exposure assessment
references.finding: All wireless baby monitors emit continuous RF. DECT monitors: 250 mW constant transmission. RF absorption approximately 10× higher in infants due to thinner skull and higher brain water content.

references.title: RF exposure from baby monitors: measurement study
references.finding: RF exposure from baby monitors within 3 feet (1 m) of the infant exceeds recommended nighttime exposure limits by 300-400%.

references.title: Seasonal patterns in SIDS: United States 1980-1987
references.finding: SIDS risk greatest at age 1-4 months and during cold season. US national surveillance data 1980-1987.

references.title: Climate and SIDS incidence correlation
references.finding: SIDS incidence correlates strongly with cold-wet weather patterns across US, UK, and Australia. Cold-wet Pacific Northwest has highest SIDS rates.

references.title: Heat stress, hyperthermia and SIDS: thermoregulation and cardiovascular vulnerability
references.finding: Heat stress and hyperthermia as SIDS risk factors. Thermoregulation, cardiovascular stability, and circadian function all reach peak vulnerability at SIDS-risk age.

references.title: Neonatal seizures: pathophysiology, mechanisms, and the NKCC1/KCC2 chloride transporter switch
references.journal: Seminars in Fetal and Neonatal Medicine
references.finding: Neonatal seizures arise from excitatory GABA action due to high NKCC1/KCC2 ratio. The chloride transporter switch (NKCC1 dominant → KCC2 dominant) occurs postnatally over weeks to months, making the neonatal brain uniquely susceptible to hyperexcitability.

references.title: Bumetanide as NKCC1 blocker: restoring GABAergic inhibition in neonatal seizures
references.finding: Bumetanide blocks NKCC1 chloride importer, reducing intracellular chloride and restoring inhibitory GABA action. Effective in reducing neonatal seizure burden, demonstrating that NKCC1/KCC2 ratio directly controls neuronal excitability in the developing brain.

references.title: Status epilepticus in neonates: the undamped oscillator model
references.finding: Neonatal status epilepticus can be modeled as resonance in an undamped oscillator where excitatory GABA (NKCC1>KCC2) removes the damping term. Q-factor predicts seizure severity better than age alone.

references.title: NKCC1 and KCC2 chloride transporters: developmental expression and the GABA excitatory-to-inhibitory switch
references.finding: NKCC1 expression is high at birth and declines postnatally. KCC2 expression is low at birth and increases over the first months of life. The NKCC1>KCC2 ratio at birth results in high intracellular chloride, making GABA depolarizing (excitatory). The switch to KCC2 dominance and inhibitory GABA occurs at approximately 2-4 weeks in rodents, 2-6 months in humans.

references.title: Bed-sharing, co-sleeping, and SIDS: international comparisons and cultural context
references.finding: Countries with high co-sleeping rates (Japan, Hong Kong) have among the lowest SIDS rates globally despite high population density and EMF exposure. Cultural practices including co-sleeping, high breastfeeding rates, and continuous infant carrying provide multiple protective mechanisms.

references.title: SIDS rates in Japan: epidemiological analysis and cultural protective factors
references.finding: Japan SIDS rate of 0.09/1000 live births is among the world lowest. Three cultural factors are protective: near-universal co-sleeping (futon, no baby monitor needed), breastfeeding rates >95%, and traditional infant carrying practices (onbu) providing continuous skin contact.

references.title: KCNQ2 mutations and neonatal seizures: spontaneous remission at 3-6 months correlates with KCC2 maturation
references.finding: KCNQ2 (Kv7.2) mutations cause benign familial neonatal seizures with characteristic spontaneous remission at 3-6 months of age. The remission timeline correlates precisely with KCC2 chloride transporter maturation and the transition of GABA from excitatory to inhibitory, suggesting seizure cessation reflects restoration of neural damping.

references.title: Prenatal radiofrequency electromagnetic field exposure and neurodevelopmental outcomes: prospective birth cohort
references.finding: Prospective birth cohort with prenatal RF-EMF exposure assessment. Higher prenatal EMF exposure associated with fine motor delay (OR 2.74, 95% CI 1.16-6.49) and problem-solving delay (OR 3.67, 95% CI 1.39-9.73) at 36 months. Dose-response relationship observed across exposure quartiles.
